clue.text: Arrogant views of bitches?

definitions.meaning: opinions laid down as beyond question, held with overbearing certainty
read as '...', mothers among the canine kind, hence the question mark

explanation.definitionFit: Dogmas are doctrines asserted without room for dispute; split in two the word jokily gives mother dogs.

clue.text: Diana-smart little bird

parts.note: Di is short for Diana
dapper means neatly dressed

explanation.surface: Diana, a neat little bird of a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The didapper is an old name for the dabchick, a small grebe.

clue.text: State game coming up for wicket-keeper

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters rise, read from the bottom up

parts.note: to state is to name
tag is a children's chasing game

explanation.surface: A cricket announcement that the wicket-keeper is coming in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns NAMETAG round. The cricket wicket-keeper is a red herring: a wicket is a small gate.
explanation.definitionFit: A wicket is a small gate, so its keeper is the person who attends a gate.

clue.text: Rebuilding Pisa ? ..Short, their pronouncements

indicators.note: the leaning tower town is being rebuilt, so its letters are rearranged with the next word

explanation.surface: A comment on restoring the leaning tower, followed by a terse remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rebuilding' rearranges PISA and SHORT; the whole clue then describes the people meant: their pronouncements are short.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphorists coin pithy maxims, brief sayings.

clue.text: Strike for a bit knocked off the pay?

definitions.text: a bit knocked off the pay?
definitions.meaning: an amount deducted from wages, in British usage

explanation.definitionFit: A strike is a halt in work, and in Britain a deduction withheld from wages is also called by this name.

clue.text: Give cue for Nick's entry

parts.note: Old Nick is the devil; a phrase said just as the person mentioned walks in serves as his cue

explanation.surface: A stage instruction to cue an actor named Nick.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Nick is a name for the devil; the saying is used when someone you were discussing appears.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is said when someone appears just as they are being discussed.

clue.text: Feeling honoured to be an upper-class drop-out

indicators.note: out means put out of place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Being pleased to be a toff who has quit society.
explanation.definitionFit: Pride is the feeling of being gratified and honoured.

clue.text: Stag hunter

definitions.meaning: a male deer, the form he was changed into
the mythical huntsman who saw Artemis bathing

explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Actaeon, a huntsman, was turned into a stag by Artemis and killed by his own hounds.

clue.text: Contingencies of free play in two quarters

indicators.note: the free play sits in between the two quarters

parts.note: E and S are east and south, two compass quarters
to give vent is to give free play to a feeling

explanation.surface: Unforeseen events in a game split into quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Contingencies are possible happenings, things that may occur.

clue.text: Tributes to victorious generals? They've all been paid

definitions.meaning: acclaim for commanders after a war is won
the wartime tax credits were refunded in later decades

explanation.definitionFit: Post-war credits were extra wartime income tax promised back after the war; jokily they are praise for winning generals.

clue.text: Plaything of a guy in Amsterdam

definitions.text: Plaything of a guy in Amsterdam

parts.words: Plaything of a guy in Amsterdam
parts.note: a toy, or a girlfriend, belonging to a man from the Netherlands

explanation.surface: A Dutchman's toy, or perhaps his girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: A wooden jointed doll from the Netherlands; 'doll' is also slang for a man's girlfriend, so the 'guy' reading doubles up.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a cheap jointed wooden toy figure traditionally associated with the Netherlands.

clue.text: The course of true love not running smooth ? Odd!

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: Shakespeare's line about a course that never did run smooth signals these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean lament about troubled romance ends with an exclamation at its strangeness.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface quotes 'the course of true love never did run smooth' from A Midsummer Night's Dream; 'The course of' is link padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Something outré is bizarre or eccentric, beyond the bounds of the usual.

clue.text: Dog to worry fish

parts.note: a Pom is a Pomeranian, a small dog breed
to fret is to worry

explanation.surface: A dog is set to harass a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The pomfret is a species of edible sea fish.

clue.text: Characters, square type, in a scrap

parts.note: characters are eccentrics, odd men
a draughtsman's T-square is the type of square named after a letter

explanation.surface: A printer's description of letters and type, set in a fragment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' and 'square type' suggest printing (letters, an em), but the characters are odd men and the square is a T-square.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddment is a leftover fragment or remnant, a bit left over.

clue.text: Birds offend an important playboy ?

indicators.note: read as 'off end', meaning the final letter is knocked off

parts.note: the man-about-town of Wilde's The Importance of Being Earnest goes by the name Ernest

explanation.surface: Some birds give offence to a notable man-about-town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offend' must be split as 'off end'. The 'important' playboy comes from Wilde's play title, where Jack calls himself Ernest in town.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernes are sea eagles, large birds of prey.

clue.text: Craft, one without mechanics

parts.note: a craft or skill is an art
I is the Roman numeral for one
sans is the French-derived word for without

explanation.surface: A craft practised by someone with no mechanical help.
explanation.definitionFit: Artisans are skilled manual workers, as mechanics once meant manual labourers.

clue.text: Army rescue op

parts.note: a mission by the Christian charity army, or a deliverance

explanation.surface: Soldiers carry out a rescue operation.
explanation.walkthrough: The Salvation Army is a Christian charity organised like an army; the word itself means rescue.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvation means rescue or deliverance from harm, and names the Christian charity army.

clue.text: Backs whose famous ride round the pole ?

indicators.note: the rider's name goes round the pole letter

parts.note: Revere's: Paul Revere's famous midnight ride of 1775
S is the south pole

explanation.surface: A question about a famous horse ride going round a pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts S inside REVERES (Revere's, the possessive needing no apostrophe in the letters). Paul Revere rode to warn of British troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverses are backward movements, as a car backs up.

clue.text: State port of Israel in liquidation

parts.note: Mass. is the abbreviation for Massachusetts, a US state
Acre is a port on Israel's northern coast

explanation.surface: An Israeli port's affairs being wound up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liquidation' reads as company winding-up but means wholesale killing.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquidation is a euphemism for killing, and a massacre is slaughter on a large scale.

clue.text: Fearful about a bad cheque marking? Granted

indicators.note: the fearful word goes about the other pieces

parts.note: awed means filled with fear or wonder
RD, refer to drawer, is the bank's marking on a bounced cheque

explanation.surface: Someone nervous about a bounced cheque is reassured.
explanation.walkthrough: RD stands for 'refer to drawer', written by a British bank on a cheque it will not honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Something awarded has been granted or bestowed.

clue.text: What to do with the bottle on the chimley piece, said Mrs Gamp

definitions.text: What to do with the bottle on the chimley piece, said Mrs Gamp

parts.words: What to do with the bottle on the chimley piece, said Mrs Gamp
parts.note: Dickens's tippling nurse in Martin Chuzzlewit asks that the bottle be put on the mantelpiece and left there for her

explanation.surface: Dickens's gin-loving nurse gives instructions about her bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: Sairey Gamp, the gin-loving nurse in Dickens's Martin Chuzzlewit, asks that the bottle be put on the mantelpiece and that she be allowed to sip from it; chimley is her dialect for chimney.
explanation.definitionFit: To let something stay where it is put is to not move it, as Mrs Gamp wants for her bottle.

clue.text: Aram's neighbour ?

parts.note: read as 'a ram is', a ram being an animal that butts; also someone living next door

explanation.surface: A question about who lives next to Aram.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Aram's' as 'a ram is': a ram is one who butts. The question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: One whose land borders another's is a neighbour; a ram is one that butts.

clue.text: Row behind us

parts.note: the rump is the behind

explanation.surface: A row breaks out behind us.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumpus is a noisy disturbance or argument.

clue.text: Ignorant girl goes to Hertfordshire town

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
Ware is a market town in Hertfordshire, a county north of London

explanation.surface: A girl who doesn't know much heads off to a Home Counties town.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unaware means lacking knowledge of something, ignorant of it.

clue.text: No British gunners upset by Hitler's paragon

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters are turned upside down, read from the bottom

parts.note: nay means no
RA is the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: No British artillerymen were upset by the Nazi ideal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nazis held up a supposed master race as their racial ideal.

clue.text: One safely placed lady holding a rod

indicators.note: the lady's name wraps around the other pieces as if holding them

parts.note: Eve is the first lady
a billiard cue is a long rod

explanation.surface: A woman holds a stick to keep herself safe.
explanation.walkthrough: Eve, the first woman, is the crossword's stock lady; the definition recalls wartime children sent away from cities.
explanation.definitionFit: An evacuee is a person moved away from danger, such as a wartime child sent to the country.

clue.text: Irish type cereal

definitions.meaning: a familiar nickname for an Irishman
rice, especially growing in a flooded field

explanation.definitionFit: Paddy is slang for an Irishman, and also means rice in the husk or the field it grows in.

clue.text: Begins at home with vermouth-is tea out ?

parts.note: in means at home
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone at home with a vermouth asks whether the tea has run out.
explanation.definitionFit: To initiate something is to start it off.

clue.text: African danseuse in make-, up

indicators.note: make-up as composition signals the letters are made up again

explanation.surface: A ballet dancer from Africa is wearing her stage make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in make-up' reorders the letters of DANSEUSE, a female ballet dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sudanese person is one from Sudan, a country in north-east Africa.

clue.text: Twists (sounds nasty)

explanation.definitionFit: Snarls are tangles in hair or rope, and a snarl is also an angry growl.
